name: L9110S dual motor driver module
//: The blue two-channel breakout, also sold as HG7881: two SOP-8 chips, green screw terminals marked MOTOR A / MOTOR B, and a 6-pin header. What a host board has to provide is under `needs`; what is true of the part is under `facts`, each with where it came from.
//needs: What this part asks of the host, and the ONLY part of this file with a fixed shape. `signal` is the name the host will use; `pin` is what the module calls it. `needs` is what the host pin must be able to do, in the vocabulary assign_pins.py understands.

needs.note: PWM-capable host pin; direction and speed both live on the two inputs
the other half of the same channel

power.note: 2.5-12 V; this is the MOTOR supply, not logic

unused_pins.note: channel B is unused in a one-motor design and must not float — tie it to the driver's own ground

//facts: Deliberately open-ended. A motor driver's facts are input thresholds and current; a rangefinder's are an I2C address and a calibration. Forcing them into one schema produces a field nobody reads. Every entry says where it came from, and `verified` is false until someone has actually checked.

input_high_threshold_v.why_it_matters: ABSOLUTE, not ratiometric. If it were 0.7 x VCC it would be 4.2 V on a 6 V supply and 3.3 V logic would never turn the motor. This was checked precisely because the ratiometric reading would have killed the design.

has_enable_pin.source: the module's own header: BIA BIB GND VCC AIA AIB
has_enable_pin.why_it_matters: There is no enable and no separate PWM pin, so the firmware has to encode direction and speed in the two inputs together.

//host_requirements: Things the host board must do that are not pins. Prose on purpose: these are design rules, and a rule nobody can read is not enforced.
host_requirements: Pull both inputs down in HARDWARE. The host's pins float for the ~300 ms between reset and firmware, and through any crash or reflash, and a floating CMOS input on an H-bridge can turn both halves on.

If a current shunt sits in this module's ground return, the module judges its inputs against ITS OWN ground, which the shunt lifts. Effective input high becomes (host logic level - I x R_shunt), and the margin over 2.5 V is what decides whether the motor turns under load.

body_mm.//: Real, measured. The header is along one 29 mm edge and the screw terminals along the opposite one, so the body is NOT centred on the header.
